metaData.title: Musk's 'One-Man Dynasty' Rings the Bell on June 12
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: SpaceX has officially filed its S-1 to launch an IPO, planning to go public on June 12 with a target valuation of $1.75 trillion to $2 trillion. Musk controls 85% of voting power through a multi-class stock structure. Starlink is the cash cow, xAI is a money-burning black hole, and the AI + aerospace narrative supports the ultra-high valuation.
metaData.summary: This article is Tencent Tech's in-depth analysis of SpaceX's IPO prospectus. It breaks down SpaceX's financial hand: Starlink generated $11.4 billion in revenue in 2025, making it the only business unit with positive cash flow, though user ARPU continues to decline. xAI lost $6.4 billion in 2025, burning approximately $1 billion per month, far exceeding OpenAI and Anthropic. Through Class B super-voting shares, Musk controls about 85% of voting power, leaving public shareholders with virtually no say post-IPO. The article also reveals the Terafab chip project, an exclusive option to acquire Cursor for $60 billion, and long-term plans like a space AI computing module. Wall Street is sharply divided on this IPO, with Goldman Sachs leading the underwriting, but some analysts see significant valuation bubble risks.

mainPoints.point: SpaceX's IPO is the largest in human history, with a target valuation of $1.75 trillion to $2 trillion.
mainPoints.explanation: The company plans to list on Nasdaq on June 12, raising $70 billion to $80 billion, with a valuation multiple of 266 times EBITDA, far exceeding Meta, Nvidia, and Tesla.

mainPoints.point: Starlink is the cash cow, xAI is a money-burning black hole, creating a financial tale of two extremes.
mainPoints.explanation: In 2025, Starlink contributed $4.4 billion in operating profit, while xAI lost $6.4 billion, with the AI business burning about $1 billion per quarter, far surpassing competitors.

mainPoints.point: Musk controls 85% of voting power through a multi-class stock structure, maintaining absolute control even after the IPO.
mainPoints.explanation: Class B common stock carries 10 votes per share. Musk holds about 42.5% of equity but controls 85% of voting power, allowing him to unilaterally decide board composition and major decisions.

mainPoints.point: The AI + aerospace narrative is the core support for the valuation, but long-term plans have no revenue or technology prototypes yet.
mainPoints.explanation: The acquisition of xAI adds a $250 billion valuation premium. The Terafab chip project, space AI computing module, and space mining plans are all in early stages, forming the most contentious part of the valuation.

keyQuotes: The money earned in the sky is all burned by the large models on the ground.

SpaceX is entering the public market at a valuation multiple more than double that of Tesla. Whether this is value discovery or a bubble narrative will be the first test the market poses after listing.
Going public just adds a bunch of passengers without voting rights; there's still only one person in the cockpit.
Goldman Sachs calls this IPO a once-in-a-generation opportunity, but some analysts compare it to buying a lottery ticket—the grand prize is Mars, the consolation prize is Earth.

relatedArticles.title: Why Did Hermes Take Over from OpenClaw in Just Two Months?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth comparison between the rising open-source AI Agent star Hermes and its predecessor OpenClaw, arguing that Hermes' success stems not from functional superiority but from encapsulating decision complexity—such as skill auto-evolution and proactive memory management—within underlying deterministic rules. This engineering safety net allowed it to deliver an automated 'gets better with use' experience precisely when the underlying technology was just barely sufficient.
